findings.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_ env check uses optional chaining, risking broken build-time inlining
findings.desc: `process.env?.NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS === "1"` uses optional chaining on `process.env`; Next.js's webpack `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` inlining relies on matching the literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X` member-expression pattern, and this documented enablement path (`NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1`) may silently fail to be replaced at build time, leaving the env-based toggle non-functional in production bundles.

findings.title: Manifest parser silently drops malformed array entries instead of failing loud
findings.desc: `parseManifest` filters `sources`/`artifacts` with `.filter(isObject)` and `customTypeIds` with `.filter(x => typeof x === "string")` before validating required fields — non-object/non-string entries are silently discarded rather than triggering `fail()`, contradicting the file's own stated "FAIL-LOUD" contract (and the codec-contract docstring) that malformed manifest data must never be silently dropped/defaulted, since that would mask data loss.

findings.title: `"not-found"` error kind is defined but never produced by any implementation
findings.desc: `CorpusErrorKind` includes `{ kind: "not-found"; path: string }`, but `opfsAdapter.ts` (and the in-memory fake) return `null` for missing files/stats rather than throwing this kind anywhere in this diff — any exhaustive consumer switch must handle a variant that can never actually occur from the shipped implementations, which is misleading documentation-by-type.
